t: Which of the following is treated as a NON-standard proof of age by Indian life insurers?
e: Horoscopes, ration cards and self-declarations are non-standard age proofs attracting restrictions or extra scrutiny; passport, school certificates and PAN are standard.

t: A proposer was born on 10 January 1990 and signs the proposal on 1 October 2026. His age 'nearer birthday' and age 'last birthday' are respectively:
e: On 1 October 2026 he completed 36 years on 10 January 2026; as more than six months have passed since that birthday, age nearer birthday is 37.

t: In a block of policies, expected deaths according to the mortality table were 200 and actual deaths were 230. The mortality ratio (actual to expected) is:
e: Mortality ratio = actual deaths / expected deaths × 100 = 230/200 × 100 = 115%, i.e., 15% extra mortality over the standard table.

t: Under the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 and IRDAI guidance, a life insurer:
o: Is prohibited from asking any question about HIV in the proposal form
Must accept every HIV-positive proposer at standard rates
Must decline every HIV-positive proposer automatically
Cannot reject a proposal solely on the ground of HIV-positive status without a proper underwriting assessment
e: The law prohibits discrimination in insurance on HIV status alone; insurers may underwrite the risk on its merits (CD4 count, treatment, viral load) and offer suitable terms.

t: Underwriting of an Accidental Death Benefit (ADB) rider focuses mainly on:
o: The proposer's occupation, avocations and accident exposure
The proposer's blood pressure and cholesterol
The proposer's family history of diabetes
e: ADB pays only on accidental death, so hazards of occupation and hobbies dominate; medical factors matter more for the base cover and critical illness riders.

t: Which of the following is NOT a usual criterion for 'preferred' (better-than-standard) risk classification?
o: Non-use of tobacco for the specified period
Blood pressure and cholesterol within preferred limits
No parent or sibling with early cardiovascular death
e: Preferred classes are based on measurable mortality factors such as tobacco use, BMI, blood pressure, lipids and family history, not educational qualifications.

t: A urine cotinine test is used by life insurers to detect:
o: Recent use of tobacco or nicotine products
e: Cotinine is a metabolite of nicotine; a positive test contradicts a non-smoker declaration and justifies smoker rates.

t: Under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938, an insurer may assume risk only when:
o: The premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed to be paid in the prescribed manner
The proposer has completed one month of good health
The agent has countersigned the proposal
The policy document has been printed
e: Section 64VB bars assumption of risk before premium receipt; this is why cover usually starts from the date of acceptance and realisation of the first premium.

t: A flat extra of ₹5 per thousand is charged for an underground mine worker on a sum assured of ₹20 lakh. The annual extra premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). ₹5 × (20,00,000 / 1,000) = ₹5 × 2,000 = ₹10,000 per annum.

t: A proposer paid the first premium by cheque on 5 March; the proposal was accepted on 10 March and the cheque was realised on 12 March. When does the risk normally commence?
o: On the date the policy bond is dispatched
On the date the proposal form was signed
On acceptance of the risk and realisation of the premium, i.e., not before 12 March
On 5 March, when the cheque was handed over
e: Section 64VB requires premium to be received (realised) before risk is assumed; mere receipt of a cheque is not payment until it is honoured.

t: A proposal exceeds the insurer's retention limit and the extra risk exceeds the automatic treaty terms. The underwriter should:
o: Issue the policy and inform the reinsurer later
Reduce the sum assured without informing the proposer
Refer the case to the reinsurer for facultative acceptance before giving a final decision
e: Risks outside treaty limits cannot be bound automatically; facultative placement must be confirmed before acceptance.

t: A 55-year-old proposer with annual income of ₹5 lakh applies for term cover of ₹2 crore (40 times income). The underwriter should regard this primarily as:
o: A preferred risk because the premium is small
A possible case of over-insurance or speculation requiring justification and verification
A case needing only a medical examination
A standard case because term plans carry no savings element
e: Income multiples fall with age (fewer earning years), so 40 times income at 55 is far beyond need and signals anti-selection or moral hazard.

t: Why does the proposal form ask for details of existing life insurance and pending proposals with other insurers?
o: To decide the policyholder's bonus entitlement
So that the underwriter can aggregate total cover and judge whether it is financially justified
e: Financial underwriting is based on total cover across all insurers; concealment of other policies is material non-disclosure.

t: For a high-net-worth proposer with little salaried income but large assets, the sum assured may be justified on the basis of:
o: The number of dependants multiplied by ₹1 lakh
Estate and business continuity needs, including net worth and liabilities
e: Net-worth-based underwriting considers estate liquidity, business value and debts where income multiples are inadequate.

t: The permitted multiple of annual income for life cover generally decreases with the proposer's age because:
o: Fewer earning years remain and the economic loss on death is smaller
e: Human Life Value depends on remaining earning years; a 25-year-old may be allowed 20-25 times income, a 55-year-old perhaps 5-10 times.

t: A 42-year-old with annual income of ₹12 lakh is allowed 15 times income. He already has cover of ₹50 lakh with another insurer. The additional cover that can be justified is:
e: Total justified cover = 15 × ₹12 lakh = ₹1.8 crore; less existing ₹50 lakh = ₹1.3 crore additional.

t: A proposer is employed as a security contractor in an active conflict zone abroad. The most likely underwriting decision is:
o: Accept only under the non-medical scheme
Postpone or decline, or accept with a substantial flat extra and war-risk exclusion, depending on the insurer's guidelines
Accept with a female age set-back
Standard acceptance because he is salaried
e: Residence or work in war zones carries a direct and unpredictable accident/violence hazard that treaty terms often exclude.

t: Long-distance truck drivers are often rated higher than their accident risk alone would suggest because:
o: The occupation is associated with lifestyle hazards such as irregular sleep, substance use and poor health care
They are usually over 60 years of age
e: Underwriting considers the environment and habits typical of an occupation, not just accident exposure.

t: Under a 40% quota share treaty, on a policy with sum assured ₹50 lakh the reinsurer's share is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Quota share cedes a fixed percentage of every risk: 40% × ₹50 lakh = ₹20 lakh.

t: Merchant navy personnel are usually underwritten with reference to:
o: The number of ports visited in a year
Rank, type of vessel (e.g., tanker, fishing) and the nature of duties on board
e: Seafaring risk varies widely: deck officers on large vessels are near standard, while fishing vessels and tankers carry higher accident hazard.

t: A radiology technician is best underwritten by assessing:
o: Adherence to safety protocols and radiation monitoring (e.g., film badge) and any evidence of over-exposure
e: Radiation exposure is a health hazard; modern safety practices usually allow standard rates when exposure is monitored and within limits.

t: Under facultative reinsurance, the cedant may bind the risk:
o: Only if the sum assured is below retention
Only after the reinsurer has confirmed acceptance of the specific case
Immediately, as the reinsurer is bound by the treaty
e: Facultative reinsurance is optional for both parties; the reinsurer can decline, so acceptance must precede issue.

t: A facultative-obligatory (fac-ob) treaty is one where:
o: The reinsurer chooses which risks to accept and the cedant must cede them
Both parties are free to accept or reject each risk
The cedant may choose which risks to cede, but the reinsurer is obliged to accept those ceded within the treaty terms
All risks are ceded automatically with no choice
e: Fac-ob gives the cedant flexibility while binding the reinsurer, so it is usually priced higher than a pure surplus treaty.

t: A newly licensed life insurer with limited capital is most likely to prefer which form of reinsurance?
o: No reinsurance until it has 1 lakh policies
Quota share, which shares every risk and provides commission and financing support for new business strain
e: Quota share reduces capital strain and transfers a steady share of risk, while reinsurers' commission helps fund acquisition costs.

t: Under original-terms (coinsurance) reinsurance, the reinsurer usually:
o: Issues a separate policy to the policyholder
Pays a reinsurance commission to the cedant to cover acquisition costs
Charges the cedant a commission for accepting the risk
Collects premium directly from the policyholder
e: Because the cedant pays agents' commission and expenses on the whole premium, the reinsurer refunds a share through reinsurance commission.

t: Polycythaemia vera is of concern to the underwriter mainly because:
o: It is a benign condition requiring no rating
It causes severe bleeding from minor injuries
The increased red cell mass raises blood viscosity and the risk of thrombosis and stroke
e: Polycythaemia vera is a myeloproliferative disorder with thrombotic risk and possible leukaemic transformation; it is rated according to control and complications.

t: Mild iron-deficiency anaemia in a 28-year-old woman with heavy menstrual periods, treated with iron, is usually:
o: Accepted at standard rates once the cause is identified and treatment is under way
e: In menstruating women iron deficiency is common and benign; in a man or an older woman, unexplained anaemia needs investigation for gastrointestinal blood loss or malignancy.

t: A company proposes keyman insurance on its CEO, whose annual compensation is ₹30 lakh. If the insurer allows 10 times compensation, the maximum keyman cover is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Keyman cover is commonly limited to a multiple of compensation (e.g., 10 times) or of the company's average profits; 10 × ₹30 lakh = ₹3 crore.

t: Uncomplicated migraine, with no neurological deficit, is usually underwritten as:
e: Migraine does not materially affect mortality; only migraine with neurological complications or suspicion of another cause needs further evaluation.

t: A proposer had a head injury with loss of consciousness in a road accident eight months ago and has fully recovered with no seizures. The usual approach is:
o: Accept at standard rates after a short postponement period provided there are no sequelae such as epilepsy
Decline because of risk of brain tumour
Insist on a lien for the entire term
e: Post-traumatic epilepsy is the main concern after head injury; once a suitable period passes without seizures, standard terms are usual.

t: A woman had gestational diabetes during her pregnancy two years ago; a recent post-partum glucose tolerance test is normal. She is usually:
o: Accepted at standard rates, noting the higher lifetime risk of developing Type 2 diabetes
e: Gestational diabetes resolves after delivery; a normal subsequent test allows standard terms, though future risk of Type 2 diabetes is raised.

t: Sugar detected in a routine urine test (glycosuria) at the medical examination should be followed by:
o: Blood glucose tests (fasting, post-prandial and/or HbA1c) to confirm or exclude diabetes
Standard acceptance since urine tests are unreliable
e: Glycosuria may be benign (renal glycosuria) or indicate diabetes; blood tests establish the diagnosis before any rating.

t: A Type 2 diabetic who has recently been switched from oral drugs to insulin is generally rated more heavily because:
o: Insulin treatment is illegal without IRDAI approval
The need for insulin in Type 2 diabetes usually indicates longer duration, declining pancreatic function or poor control
e: Progression to insulin reflects more advanced disease; underwriters also consider hypoglycaemia-related accident risk for riders.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is:
o: An autoimmune condition that is the commonest cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas
A congenital absence of the thyroid gland
A viral infection causing temporary hyperthyroidism
A malignant tumour of the thyroid
e: Hashimoto's leads to gradual thyroid failure; once treated with thyroxine it is usually standard.

t: The single most useful screening test for thyroid dysfunction is:
e: TSH is highly sensitive to both over- and under-activity of the thyroid and is the first-line test; T3/T4 follow if TSH is abnormal.

t: Adult polycystic kidney disease is of concern to underwriters because:
o: It is caused by excessive water intake
It is an inherited (autosomal dominant) condition that commonly progresses to hypertension and renal failure
It resolves spontaneously by middle age
e: Progressive cyst formation destroys kidney tissue; ratings depend on renal function, blood pressure and age, with advanced cases declined.

t: A person who donated a kidney to a relative five years ago and has normal function in the remaining kidney is usually:
o: Declined because of a single kidney
Accepted at standard rates or with a small extra
e: Living donors are carefully screened and have near-normal life expectancy; the remaining kidney compensates adequately.

t: Sarcoidosis that resolved completely without lung function impairment is usually:
o: Accepted at standard rates after a suitable period
e: Sarcoidosis is a granulomatous disease that often resolves; chronic cases with pulmonary fibrosis, cardiac or neurological involvement are rated or declined.

t: A 45-year-old smoker with 25 pack-years has an FEV1 of 55% of predicted. His COPD would be graded and underwritten as:
o: Moderate COPD, warranting a substantial extra mortality rating
Not COPD at all since he is under 50
e: FEV1 50-79% predicted is moderate (GOLD 2) COPD; continued smoking worsens the outlook and the rating.

t: A proposer underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallstones one year ago with complete recovery. The usual decision is:
e: Removal of the gallbladder cures gallstone disease; there is no residual mortality risk.

t: Ulcerative colitis of long standing is relevant to the underwriter because:
o: Extensive, long-duration disease increases the risk of colorectal cancer and may need surgery
It is always cured with one course of antibiotics
e: Underwriting depends on extent, activity, treatment (steroids, immunosuppressants, colectomy) and surveillance; quiescent limited disease may be near standard.

t: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is particularly significant in young proposers because:
o: It is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death in young people and athletes
It is a form of hypertension
It is always cured by antibiotics
It only causes mild chest discomfort
e: HCM is often inherited and carries arrhythmic risk; such cases are heavily rated or declined.

t: A proposer diagnosed with congestive heart failure would normally be:
o: Accepted with a flat extra of ₹1 per mille
e: Heart failure carries very high mortality regardless of cause; it is uninsurable for life cover in most cases.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

t: A normal left ventricular ejection fraction on echocardiography is approximately:
e: EF below 40% indicates significant systolic dysfunction and attracts heavy ratings; normal EF is 55-70%.

t: Which of the following is a NON-modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease?
o: Family history of premature heart disease
e: Age, male sex and family history cannot be changed; smoking, lipids, blood pressure, diabetes and inactivity are modifiable.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Severe bilateral deafness in a proposer is generally underwritten as:
o: Standard for life cover, with consideration of accident risk for riders and in hazardous occupations
e: Deafness itself does not shorten life; the cause (e.g., meningitis sequelae) and accident exposure are what the underwriter checks.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Chronic suppurative otitis media (CSOM) that has been treated surgically with no complications is usually:
e: CSOM historically risked intracranial spread of infection, but treated cases carry no extra mortality today.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Hypertensive retinopathy of advanced grade (haemorrhages, exudates or papilloedema) seen on fundus examination indicates:
o: Severe hypertension with end-organ damage, warranting a heavy rating or declinature
e: The retina mirrors the small vessels of the body; advanced hypertensive retinopathy correlates with kidney and heart damage.
